content.articleInstructions:
All content must strictly adhere to the defined BLOG_RULES outlined below. Any deviation is not acceptable.

1. TONE & VOICE (STRICT)

Maintain a professional, calm, and educational tone

Content must be non-alarmist and factual

Do not use fear-based, urgent, or sensational language

Avoid exaggerated risk statements (e.g., “extremely dangerous,” “guaranteed failure”)

Write for homebuyers and homeowners, not contractors

Position the inspector as an educator, not a problem-solver

2. LIABILITY & LEGAL SAFETY (STRICT)

❌ No DIY instructions or step-by-step fixes

❌ No repair advice or recommendations

❌ No code enforcement, compliance orders, or legal interpretations

❌ No statements implying inspection guarantees or liability transfer

Allowed language examples:

“may be associated with”

“is commonly observed”

“can be evaluated further by a qualified professional”

“often noted during home inspections”

Disallowed language examples:

“must be repaired immediately”

“violates code”

“illegal”

“fix this by”

“required to replace”

3. STRUCTURE & EDUCATIONAL COMPLIANCE

Use clear H2 and H3 headings throughout

Include a dedicated “Relevant Standards” section in every article

Relevant Standards Section Rules:

Reference IRC and NEC strictly for educational context

Do not cite specific code sections as violations

Do not imply enforcement authority

Present standards as general industry guidance only

Example phrasing:

“According to commonly referenced guidance within the IRC and NEC, certain conditions are generally evaluated during inspections for safety and performance considerations.”

4. SCOPE CLARITY

Clearly state that a home inspection is visual and non-invasive

Emphasize that inspectors identify conditions, not outcomes

Avoid predictions, warranties, or performance guarantees

5. BRAND POSITIONING

Reinforce Inspection Time as:

Knowledgeable

Neutral

Buyer-focused

Inspection-only (not repair or construction)

6. FINAL CHECK BEFORE SUBMISSION

Before final output, verify:

Tone is professional and neutral

No DIY or enforcement language exists

Relevant Standards section is present

Inspector role is clearly defined as observational and educational
